entries.title: Abu Hanifa
entries.summary: Abu Hanifa was a foundational jurist of Kufa whose legal school (Hanafi) became one of the major Sunni madhhabs.
entries.detailed_information: Working in a period of rapid social change, Abu Hanifa emphasized reasoned legal analogy within Qur'an and Sunnah frameworks according to classical accounts of his method. His students spread Hanafi jurisprudence widely, especially later under Abbasid and Ottoman contexts.
entries.historical_significance: Eponym of a major Islamic legal tradition.

entries.title: Al-Ghazali
entries.summary: Abu Hamid al-Ghazali was a major theologian, jurist, and spiritual writer whose works reshaped Sunni thought and engagement with philosophy.
entries.detailed_information: Associated with the Nizamiyya milieu, al-Ghazali wrote critiques of certain philosophical positions, defenses of Sunni theology, and the influential Ihya Ulum al-Din. His career included a famous spiritual crisis and withdrawal from teaching, later returning to writing and guidance.
entries.historical_significance: Central figure in classical Islamic intellectual and spiritual history.
related_questions: What was the role of madrasas?

entries.title: Ibn Rushd (Averroes)
entries.summary: Ibn Rushd was an Andalusi philosopher, jurist, and physician famous for commentaries on Aristotle and debates on reason and revelation.
entries.detailed_information: Serving as a qadi and physician, Ibn Rushd wrote extensive Aristotelian commentaries that later influenced Latin European scholasticism (as Averroes). He engaged arguments associated with al-Ghazali regarding philosophy. His career also faced political-religious pressures in the Almohad context.
entries.historical_significance: Bridge figure between Islamic philosophy and medieval European thought.

entries.title: Ibn Khaldun
entries.summary: Ibn Khaldun was a North African historian and social theorist whose Muqaddimah pioneered analytical historiography and concepts of group solidarity (asabiyya).
entries.detailed_information: Ibn Khaldun served in various political roles across the Maghrib and Egypt. His Muqaddimah examines rise and fall of dynasties, urban-rural dynamics, and methods of historical criticism. He is often cited as a forerunner of sociology and philosophy of history.
entries.historical_significance: Landmark figure in the theory and method of history writing.
related_questions: What cultural developments shaped late medieval Islam?
